category: hosted feature flags with flat per-plan pricing

free_tier.stated: Free plan, USD 0 a month, free forever, no credit card: 10 flags per project, 2 environments per project, 1 project, up to 3 team members, 7-day audit logs, 1 webhook endpoint, Management API access, community support; unlimited flag evaluations
free_tier.notes: The plan is a flat monthly price with none of seats, monthly active users or evaluations metered. Flags per project is the count of active flags; archiving a flag frees its place. The next plan, Team, is USD 49 a month (USD 39 annual) for 5 members, 3 projects and unlimited flags.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-flag value size cap is stated on the pricing or plans-and-limits pages read

retention.stated: 7-day audit log retention on Free; 30 days on Team and Pro; 90 days on Business; 365 days on Enterprise
retention.notes: Audit entries older than 7 days are removed in the next daily cleanup on Free. No retention period for flag values is stated on the pages read.

egress.terms: not applicable: a flag service with flat pricing and no metered evaluations or traffic allowance published

interface_detail: A Management API for flag and project operations, with an MCP server and a Terraform provider; client SDKs stream flag configuration to the application and evaluate flags locally with percentage rollouts, targeting rules and kill switches. Sign-in with Google or GitHub is available on every plan.
tooling: 14 official SDKs, the Management API, the MCP server and the Terraform provider
chaining: Run flags for a small staging and production setup in one project, using local SDK evaluation with no per-evaluation charge and no traffic meter.

limits.value: 10 active flags per project on Free
1 project, 2 environments per project and up to 3 team members on Free

limits_note: Everything else is on Free, including targeting rules, segments, percentage rollouts, all 14 SDKs, the Management API and the audit log. Over a plan ceiling, creating a new flag or project is blocked while existing flag evaluation continues. Team members include pending invitations.
binding_note: The 10 active flags per single project bind first for a growing app; evaluations are unlimited, so traffic does not consume a plan allowance.

identity_cost.detail: The sign-up form asks for Name, Email, Password, Organization Name and URL Slug, then a plan choice; the pricing page states the Free plan needs no credit card. Sign-in with Google or GitHub is available on every plan. No phone number or ID is requested on the form; whether a later step asks for one is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Over a plan ceiling, the creation of new flags or projects is blocked while existing flag evaluation continues without interruption. Scheduled changes and required two-factor authentication begin on the Team plan. The Enterprise plan is arranged with the team and adds on-premise deployment, which is software the reader runs and is the last resort.
confidence_note: Every value is quoted from the first-party pricing page, plans-and-limits documentation and sign-up page. No account was opened and no live flag evaluation was probed, so the record stays at documented rung.
